plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with golden centers. They open in the cool of winter, when little else is flowering in the garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with peak bloom from January through March in mild climates
plants.location: Japan, the southeastern United States and other mild temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Japan has cultivated it for centuries, and it is closely tied to the tea ceremony.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A twiggy tree that flowers on bare branches, sometimes among late snow. Its fragrant blossoms drift through the cold air in early winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, usually January to March
plants.location: Southern and eastern China, and Japan's warmer regions
plants.funFact: In Chinese culture the plum blossom stands for resilience and perseverance because it blooms in the harshest part of winter.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. In summer they fill gardens with blue.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer, roughly December to February
plants.location: Coastal South Africa, and Australian and New Zealand gardens
plants.funFact: Despite the common name, it is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for "love" and "flower."
